=== e6bd IMPLEMENTED (held-out oracle GREEN) + a PLAN GAP found in 7f86 ===

GATE STATE at ad5ced165 (all --ref HEAD):
  e6bd  certified/signed  (was already)
  a49e  certified/signed  (I ran review-plan; it was UNSIGNED at handoff -- the "review in
        flight" never landed an attestation, so that handoff note was optimistic)
  8229  unsigned, and NOT reviewable yet: it is blocked by e6bd, so review-plan fast-fails
        with no LLM. Review it only after e6bd closes.
  7f86  unsigned (its description was corrected at handoff, which invalidated the prior PASS
        in substance). Review running now. Claiming e6bd CASCADES to 7f86, so 7f86's
        attestation is a hard prerequisite for starting ANY child.

REVIEW ORDER MATTERS AND I FOLLOWED IT: a49e (child) BEFORE 7f86 (parent). Reviewing the
parent first and then editing a child would have invalidated the parent's pin.

e6bd IMPLEMENTATION: interpret_failure() + frozen FailureContext now live in
structured_run.py (NOT failure.py -- failure.py stays pure classification; structured_run is
the run-execution cluster and already imports usage_log). runner.py's three except arms
collapse to one `except Exception as exc: interpret_failure(exc, run_messages, ctx)`, with
isinstance dispatch inside preserving the arm order.

HELD-OUT TDD, as run: I authored 15 tests, confirmed RED, then handed the implementer ONLY
the 3 happy-path tests (physically removed the rest from the tree). It never saw the
ordering, metadata, or end-to-end cases. On restore, all 15 passed.

THE TRAP THE ORACLE WAS BUILT AROUND, recorded because it is easy to get wrong: LLMConfigError
is a SUBCLASS of LLMUnavailableError. So `isinstance(err, LLMUnavailableError)` passes even if
the sampling-parameter translation is dropped ENTIRELY and the broad arm handles it. Every
arm-ordering assertion must use `type(x) is`, never isinstance. Same shape one arm up:
UsageLimitExceeded is a plain Exception, so a broad-arm-first spine silently reclassifies a
budget stop as a provider outage.

=== PLAN GAP in 7f86, MEASURED -- resolve before trusting its arithmetic ===

7f86 says e6bd alone takes runner.py 782 -> 707, "STILL OVER" the <700 guard, and that both
extractions are needed "before the stack can push green". That is only safe if CI votes on the
final state. IT DOES NOT. .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml checks out the EXACT PATCHSET
(checkout-gerrit-change-action, gerrit-refspec refs/changes/NN/NNNN/P) and runs the full suite
per change, casting Verified per change. So an intermediate commit at 707 (or 718 measured)
gets Verified -1 and the stack CANNOT be submitted -- a red ancestor blocks the whole chain.

CONSEQUENCE: e6bd must clear 700 BY ITSELF. Pure extraction measured 718, not the 707 the plan
projected. The extra ~18 lines have to come out of run() in the same change.

MY FIRST IMPLEMENTER PASS DID THAT THE WRONG WAY and I rejected it: it hit 698 by condensing
comments in regions unrelated to the extraction, DELETING measured content -- the
anthropic.py:1611-1616 caching citation, the "no RunRequest content-list change, so the
structured-output retry path is untouched" invariant, "every model_override test pins the
string behavior", the "retry-to-exhaustion failure mode" name, and the reason cache keys are
applied only at the shared seam ("would error on an unrelated provider"). Deleting
documentation to satisfy a guard is the same species of move as raising the cap, which ADR
0056 rejects by name. Re-dispatched with an explicit rule: compress WORDING only; never drop a
measured number, a file:line citation, a bug/story id, a named failure mode, or an invariant --
and if the facts cannot fit under 700, STOP and report the gap rather than delete one.

NOTE for whoever plans 8229: the same per-patchset arithmetic applies to it. And note that
NEITHER extraction alone clears 700 from 782 (782-80=702 for 8229 too), so the ordering is not
what makes this tight -- the guard requires more than one seam's worth of relief per change.

MONKEYPATCH HAZARD DOES NOT BITE e6bd: the eight `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, "...")`
targets in the suite are _import_pydantic_ai, _local_proxy_bypass_base_url, _pai_model,
_pai_structured, cache_settings_for, capabilities_for, get_runner, ProviderSession. NONE is in
the except spine, so this child needs zero test repoints. The hazard 7f86 documents is real but
lands on the LATER children.

NOTHING PUSHED. Stack still the four unpushed commits on top of change 1104.
